applied_items.content:
Control characters. A control character is a C0 control (U+0000 to U+001F), DEL (U+007F), a C1 control (U+0080 to U+009F) or a bidirectional override or isolate (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069). Before writing any committed record, Chough SHALL refuse a value a person gives that holds one, in every field REQ-records-006 checks, as `refused:control-character`, naming the field and the character's code point and never the value, with every file byte-identical, under `--redact` too; a line feed SHALL be accepted in a field that accepts a line break, and a carriage return directly before it SHALL be dropped, so a line break pasted from Windows is stored as a line feed (#366). Chough SHALL print text it read from a record or was given, in text and JSON output alike, with each control character escaped as `\u` and four lowercase hex digits, the form JSON uses, so no terminal acts on it, while JSON output still parses back to the stored value; a line feed SHALL be printed as it is where the text is shown on several lines and as `\n` where it is shown on one line, such as the reason on `chough next`'s `Native change: none needed:` line (#366). What Chough generates from stored text, the journal feed `knowledge/journal/feed.xml`, `knowledge/index.md` and an archived story, SHALL hold that text as it is printed, so a post or a record an earlier release wrote leaves the feed well-formed XML and neither file nor the story holds a control character raw (#366). A front matter scalar that a YAML reader takes as other than text, `null`, `~`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `on` or `off` in any letter case, SHALL be written double-quoted, so every text field reads back as text (#366). Trace: LIFE-26, LIFE-3.

Acceptance Criteria
- With ESC, BEL, DEL, U+009B, U+202E and U+2066 each in an objective, a decision, a `--no-native-change` reason, a `--pr`, an evidence summary, environment and limitation, a bug title, an inbox entry and relayed `--words`, the write is refused as `refused:control-character` naming the field and the code point, the output holds no control character, and every file is unchanged, with `--redact` as well.
- A decision and an evidence summary holding a line feed are written, while one holding a tab is refused as `refused:control-character` naming U+0009; a CRLF line break is stored as a line feed; `--title` and `--pr` holding a line feed are refused as before; a tab already stored is printed as `\u0009`.
- A fixture holding each control character, written by hand as an earlier release could, in every record kind (session, story, evidence entry, bug, inbox entry, journal post, case definition and gate), and every command in `chough --help`'s tree run over it, in text and JSON where it has both, with the fixture's IDs where a command takes one: no output holds a control character raw, and each JSON output still parses; a command added later is in the sweep without editing it. A `--no-native-change` reason holding a line feed shows on `next`'s line as `\n`.
- With a journal post and a session from an earlier release holding each control character, `chough library index` writes a feed that parses as XML and an index holding none raw, and archiving the session writes a story holding none raw.
- `--no-native-change null`, `--decision true`, `--decision yes`, a blocker `Off` and an objective `~` are written double-quoted and read back as text.

No leaks in committed records. Before writing any committed record, Chough SHALL check every value it writes, in front matter and body, including recorded commands, summaries, reasons, decisions, answers to questions, relayed words and places, notes, limitations, titles, module names and actor values, for: an absolute path under a home, temporary or system root (`/Users/`, `/home/`, `/root/`, `/private/`, `/tmp/`, `/var/`, `/Volumes/`, `/mnt/`) or a Windows drive path; a `~/` or `~<user>/` path; the local host name anywhere when it is at least 8 characters long or holds a digit, a hyphen or a dot, and a shorter all-letter host name, which may be an ordinary word, only inside a path or a URL or as `<user>@<host>`, or as the `<host>:/<absolute path>` of an scp-style remote path, where the local host names are the machine's host name, its first label and, on macOS, its LocalHostName, each also as `<name>.local`, and one holding a dot counts inside a hyphenated name too, as in `build-<host>-1` (#368); and the local user name, checked as the account's name and also as each of `USER`, `LOGNAME` and `USERNAME` that is set (#379), when it appears inside an absolute path, except as the first component of one that names a system root such as `/dev/`, after `~`, or as `<user>@<host>`. A relative path or a web URL (`http:` or `https:`) holds no user name, while a local file URL (`file:`) is checked like the path it carries, and the name `root` never counts (#379); an email address; and credentials: GitHub, GitLab, Slack (bot, user, workspace and `xapp-` app tokens), AWS, Hugging Face (`hf_`) and model-provider token forms, private key blocks, bearer and basic authorization values, JSON web tokens, and `password`, `secret`, `secret_key`, `secret_access_key` (as in `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`), `token` or `api_key` assignments, with the key quoted or not, as in `{"password": …}`, and a value of 8 or more characters (#368). A value that matches SHALL refuse the write as `refused:leak`, naming the field and the kind of match and never the matched text, with every file byte-identical. With `--redact`, each match SHALL instead be replaced by `<redacted:<kind>>` and the write SHALL proceed, saying how many values were redacted, `chough evidence add` included (#368); a module name is an ID, so it is refused under `--redact` too. An error SHALL show a value a person gave, such as a session name from `--session`, `CHOUGH_SESSION` or `session use`, a bug or evidence reference or a `--decided-by` value, only when the value holds no match and no control character; otherwise it SHALL name the field and what it holds, as in `CHOUGH_SESSION holds token`, never the value (#367). Output that repeats a value given on the command line, such as the environment `chough next` and `chough status` show or the criteria, requirements and paths `chough cases select` lists, SHALL follow the same rule (#367). A human's configured display name (REQ-records-008) SHALL NOT count as a user name. `chough doctor` SHALL scan every file Git tracks under `.chough/` and `knowledge/` for the same patterns and SHALL report each as a `leak` finding with the file, the line and the kind, never the text, except that a path under `/tmp/` or `/private/tmp/` in a case definition (`.chough/cases/*.cases.toml`) is a deliberate test setting, such as a case's own `XDG_DATA_HOME`, and SHALL NOT be reported or offered `--redact`, while a home path, the local user or host name, an email or a credential in a case definition still SHALL; the verify and CI lanes SHALL run that scan and fail on a finding. An scp-style remote path, `<host>:/<absolute path>`, SHALL be checked like the path it carries, so a home or system root after the colon refuses as a path leak and the host part counts as the local host name when it matches. Trace: LIFE-26, LIFE-17, FLOW-22.

Acceptance Criteria
- Each pattern kind, placed in an evidence summary, a decision, a relayed `--words`, a bug note and a recorded command, refuses the write with `refused:leak` naming the field and kind, the output never contains the matched text, and every file is unchanged.
- The same writes with `--redact` store `<redacted:<kind>>` and report the count.
- A decision naming the configured human display name is written; the same name inside `/Users/<name>/` is refused.
- With one committed record holding a home path, `chough doctor` reports a `leak` finding with its file, line and kind, without the path, and exits 1; `fledge lanes run verify` fails on it.
- The records of a full fixture cycle run inside a temporary directory hold no absolute path, user name or host name.
- A committed case definition whose binding sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` to a path under `/tmp/` gives no `leak` finding from `chough doctor`, while one holding a home-folder path still gives one naming the file and line.
- With a short all-letter host name, a record using it as an ordinary word is written and `chough doctor` reports nothing, while the same name inside a path, a URL or as `<user>@<host>` is still refused; a host name of 8 or more characters, or one holding a digit, hyphen or dot, is still refused anywhere.
- With an scp-style remote path, `<host>:/<absolute path>`, the write is refused as a path leak when a home or system root follows the colon, and the host part is refused as a host-name leak when it is the local host, in the write guard and in `chough doctor` alike.
- `checkpoint --resolve-question <question> --answer <text>` with each pattern kind refuses with `refused:leak` naming `answer`, with every file unchanged; with `--redact` the answer holds `<redacted:<kind>>`; an answer over 4,096 bytes is refused (#364).
- `{"password": "…"}`, `SECRET_KEY=…`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…`, an `xapp-` and an `hf_` token, a `~<user>/` path, the LocalHostName's `<name>.local` and a dotted host name inside `build-<host>-1` each refuse the write; `session new --module` holding a pattern kind is refused (#368).
- With `USER` and `LOGNAME` unset, the account's user name as `<user>@<host>` is still refused; with the user named `dev`, a `/dev/…` path, `src/dev/main.rs` and `https://example.com/dev/guide` are written while `/opt/dev/x` is refused; with the account `root`, `ssh root@build-box` and `postgres://root@db/x` are written; a home path and a `~/` path are still refused (#379).
- `evidence add --redact` with a leaking value says how many values it redacted (#368).
- An unknown session, bug or evidence reference or `--decided-by` value holding a pattern kind or a control character is refused naming the field and what it holds, and the output holds neither the value nor the control character; a clean one is still named (#367).
- With the user named `dev`, `file:///opt/dev/x` is refused as a `user-name` leak, while `https://example.com/dev/guide` is still written; with `USER`, `LOGNAME` and `USERNAME` set to three names, each is refused inside an absolute path.
- A sweep that gives every value a command takes, flag or argument, a token and an escape sequence finds neither in any error or output, including `pref set` and `pref unset`, `consent revoke`, `skill status` and `skill remove-legacy` with `--host`, `stage advance --to`, `stage enter` and `stage back --to`, `validate resume`, an explicit evidence ID, `library merge`, `correct`, `next --environment`, `status --environment` and `cases select`; each names the field and what it holds instead (#367).

Canonical checkpoint. The helper SHALL keep one canonical checkpoint per open session: the front matter of the active session's `session.md` (REQ-records-004, REQ-cli-037), holding the objective, intent scope, modules, current stage with its status, iteration and side-stage callers, the native change identity, the pull request, referenced criteria, requirements, cases, design sources and files, observation and bug references, blockers, awaiting-human gates, run consents and the next action, with decisions, completed work and open questions in the story sections of the same file. `chough checkpoint --pr <number or URL>` SHALL set the pull request when the value is a pull request number, a positive whole number written without a sign or leading zero, optionally after one `#`, which is stored without it, or an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host and none of whitespace, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `<`, `>`, a quote, a backtick or a backslash, passed through the leak guard of REQ-records-006 as the field always is; it SHALL refuse any other value, naming the two forms and never the value, with the session file byte-identical, and an empty value SHALL clear it, removing `pr` from the front matter; the pull request SHALL be written as a double-quoted string, and a stored `pr: ""` SHALL read as no pull request everywhere (#353). `chough next` and `chough status`, in text and JSON, `chough context` and the checkpoint view `chough checkpoint` prints SHALL show the session's pull request when it has one, and the journal post SHALL link it only as such a number or URL, leaving out a stored value that is neither, as an earlier release could write (#353); like `--objective` and `--title`, it SHALL add no Timeline entry. No other writable checkpoint store SHALL exist and no adapter such as APS SHALL be required. Reading and saving a session SHALL refuse, with nothing written, a `no_native_change` that holds only white space or a `<placeholder>`, and one held together with a native change, so an edit of the file by hand cannot allow the ungated move; the refusal SHALL name the session file and the field and say what to edit, the real reason in place of the value or the line removed, or one of the two fields removed. An empty `no_native_change` reads as none recorded. While it is recorded and no native change is, a stage move that SpecSync's configuration would otherwise refuse as `refused:no-native-change` SHALL be allowed and labelled `ungated:no-native-change-required`, so the session can advance to done and be archived with outcome `done` (REQ-history-006), its story keeping the reason; an open human gate that holds the stage SHALL still refuse the move (REQ-cli-030), and only a person closes it. Trace: FLOW-13, LIFE-3, DRIVE-3, DRIVE-24, DRIVE-25.

Acceptance Criteria

- With SpecSync configured, `checkpoint --native-change` for an ID SpecSync does not report, or after a failed or timed-out status read, exits non-zero with `refused:native-change-unknown` or the read failure and leaves the session file byte-identical even with other updates in the same call; a reply naming a different change refuses as `refused:native-change-mismatch` with the file byte-identical; a JSON reply naming no change ID, such as `[]` or `{}`, refuses as `refused:native-change-unknown` with the file byte-identical; a reported ID saves; without SpecSync any well-formed ID saves and a malformed one is refused.
- `chough checkpoint --pr 150` and `--pr` with an `https://` pull request URL each set the session's `pr`, which another process reads back, and `--pr '#12'` stores `12`; `--pr ""` removes `pr`; `0`, `#0`, `012`, `src/pr.txt`, `not a pr`, `ftp://x/1`, `42](javascript:alert(1))`, `https://x/1)[click](javascript:alert(1)` and a value with a line break are refused naming the two forms, without the value, with the session file byte-identical; one holding a local path or a token is refused, or redacted under `--redact`; no Timeline entry is added.
- With `pr` set, `chough next`, `chough status`, `chough context` and `chough checkpoint` each show it, in text and JSON; a stored `pr` that is neither form is shown escaped (REQ-records-016) and left out of the journal post's links.
- `--pr 42` is written as `pr: "42"`; a session holding `pr: ""`, as many existing ones do, shows no pull request in `next`, `status`, `context` and the checkpoint view, and its journal post links none.
- A session file edited by hand to hold `no_native_change: " "`, or to hold both `native_change` and `no_native_change`, is refused by `chough next`, `chough checkpoint` and `chough stage advance`, naming the file, the field and the edit, with every file byte-identical; `chough session list` still lists that session as not readable with that reason and `chough session shelve <id>`, `chough doctor` still runs, and a command given another open session is unaffected.

applied_items.content:
Append-only corrections. `chough correct <entry> --reason <text>` SHALL append a `correction` entry to the timeline that holds `<entry>`, giving `corrects: ^<entry id>` and the statement, and SHALL leave every existing byte of that file unchanged, so history is never rewritten. `<entry>` SHALL be `^<entry id>` for the active session, or `<session id>#^<entry id>` for any open session or archived story, the session ID or an alias (REQ-records-003). Correcting an entry of an archived story SHALL append to that story's Timeline and change nothing else in it (REQ-records-012). It SHALL refuse, writing nothing, an unknown session or entry, a blank statement or one over 4,096 bytes, and a correction of a correction, naming a given `<entry>` only as REQ-records-006 allows, so one holding a pattern kind or a control character is named by what it holds, never echoed (#367). `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL show the corrected text of a corrected decision or next action, marked as corrected with the count of corrections, for the active session and for archived stories they show; `chough next` SHALL list at most 10 corrections, newest first by recorded time and then entry ID, each cut to 512 bytes, with their total. `chough timing` SHALL treat a correction as a known kind that starts and ends no stage segment. Trace: LIFE-18, LIFE-7, FLOW-13.

Acceptance Criteria
- Correcting a stage move's reason appends one `correction` entry linked to it, and the session file is otherwise byte-identical; `next` and `status` show the corrected text marked as corrected.
- Correcting an entry of an archived story appends to its Timeline only, and every earlier byte of the story is unchanged.
- An unknown entry, a blank or 4,097-byte statement and a correction of a correction are refused with nothing written.
- With 12 corrections, `next` lists 10 newest first and says 12 in total; `timing --json` reports no unrecognised kind.
- An `<entry>` holding a token or an escape sequence is refused with nothing written, naming what it holds, and the output holds neither.

applied_items.content:
Timing report. The helper SHALL provide a read-only timing report derived from existing records: stage segments from transitions, including iterations, back, reset, skip, pause and resume, and side-stage enter and return; case observations and repeated-run summaries; bug creation, reproduction and verification; and the native lifecycle times native SpecSync exposes. A session's `start` entry (REQ-history-002) SHALL start its first stage segment, in Cycle 1; a timeline without one, such as a migrated or older one, SHALL leave that segment's start unknown. The text report SHALL say once, in its header, that its durations are elapsed wall-clock time, and its JSON SHALL keep that label on every value; no gate-wait, segment or estimate line SHALL repeat it. It SHALL append a timestamped transition when an awaiting-human gate opens and one when it is cleared, and SHALL report active time separately from paused time and from time waiting on a human, without recording who decided or what. Every duration SHALL be labelled elapsed wall-clock time, not effort; history summaries SHALL give ranges with their sample count, labelled estimates rather than targets; a missing, unparseable or out-of-order timestamp SHALL be reported unknown, never zero. Transitions SHALL be read from each session's timeline, in open sessions and archived stories alike (REQ-history-002), and case observations, with their run times from `duration_seconds` when known, from evidence entries and the receipts of archived stories and bugs (REQ-cli-017), within the bounds of REQ-history-003; a session or story that cannot be read SHALL be named and the report marked partial. Inputs SHALL be bounded, and the report SHALL write no record. Text the report shows from a record, such as a gate's name, SHALL be printed as REQ-records-016 says, so no terminal acts on a control character in it (#366). Trace: LIFE-10, DRIVE-24, LIFE-3, LIFE-6, LIFE-7.

Acceptance Criteria
- Fixture transitions with fixed timestamps for every transition kind yield the expected segments, gate records and `direct-native-write` events (REQ-history-013) start or end no segment, a `direct-native-write` event is not counted as an unrecognised kind, and paused and waiting-on-human time are excluded from active time.
- Opening a gate appends one gate-opened transition and clearing it one gate-closed transition; the report shows its waiting time, and a gate-opened record whose gate is no longer awaiting a human, with no gate-closed record, is reported closed at an unknown time.
- A missing timestamp or an end before its start is reported unknown, not zero, and fewer than three samples are reported too few to estimate.
- Running the report leaves every Chough and SpecSync record byte-identical, and input beyond its bound is reported partial.
- With one open session and three archived stories, the report gives each session's stage segments and gate waits from its timeline and each case's runs from entries and receipts; an unreadable story is named and the report is marked partial.
- No file under `.chough/history/` or `.chough/transitions.jsonl` is read.
- After `chough init`, the timing report starts Cycle 1's first segment at the `start` entry's time, a timeline without a `start` entry leaves it unknown, and the text says elapsed wall-clock once, in its header, while the JSON labels every value.
- `chough timing`'s text says elapsed wall-clock once, in its header, and no gate-wait, segment or estimate line repeats it.
- With a gate's name holding ESC and U+202E, `chough timing` prints neither raw, in text or JSON, and its JSON parses back to the stored name.
